data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate opened 2021 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 160.9m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle for older underwriting years (<=2019) indicates overall adverse prior year development of approximately GBP 6.6m (c.4.1% of opening reserves), driven by adverse development predominantly in the 2019 and 2019/2018 diagonals, partially offset by reductions in older years. Management narrative states that favourable prior year development emerged on 2019 and 2020, benefitting from subrogation on the 2018 wildfires but partly offset by adverse development on the Cyber book. Separately, 2021 saw significant catastrophe activity (Hurricane Ida, Texas Winter Storms and European floods) with a combined net impact of GBP 33.0m and a reduced COVID-19 impact of GBP 3.6m.

The Syndicate benefitted from favourable outcomes from subrogation on the 2018 wildfires, partly offset by adverse loss development on the Syndicate's Cyber book.

The financial impact of COVID-19 on the Syndicate significantly reduced in 2021, with an overall net impact of GBP 3.6m or 2.2% of the combined ratio

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development (PYD) was not provided as a single explicit GROSS movement figure in a 'movement in prior year provision' note. PYD was calculated from the gross claims development table (claims triangle) as the preferred gross source. The narrative text states 'favourable prior year development' which appears directionally inconsistent with the triangle-derived net strengthening of +GBP 6.6m; users should note this discrepancy. No RITC distortions were identified that would invalidate the triangle, though a Part VII / LIC transfer at 30 Dec 2020 is noted in the report and may affect comparatives.
